units.tr: At the Council of Constance, an attempt was made to deprive the masters of arts and the physicians of the indult to obtain and hold great benefices. They bravely opposed the decree, and it was agreed and resolved that the privileges of the University should be common to all four Faculties.

units.la: On consulta les Jurisconsultes, pour sçavoir si les Medecins pouvoient faire des Statuts, obliger à les observer, les casser, & en dispenser : La response fut telle, qu'ils le pouvoient faire en tout ce qui concerne les affaires de la Faculté.
units.tr: The jurists were consulted as to whether physicians could make statutes, oblige others to observe them, annul them and grant dispensations from them. The response was that they could do so in all matters concerning the affairs of the Faculty.

units.la: Depuis 1391. il y a tousiours eu 32. 34. ou 36. Maistres Regens, mais quand les Anglois ont possedé la ville de Paris, ils n'estoiet que dix ou douze: les Anglois se sont introduits dans nos Escholes, & vray semblablement ont emporté auec eux nos Registres, & Livres, ou bien se sont égarez, quand nos Medecins ont abandonné Paris.
units.tr: Since 1391 there have always been 32, 34 or 36 regent masters; but when the English held the city of Paris, there were only ten or twelve. The English forced their way into our Schools, and it is very likely that they carried off with them our registers and books, or else they were lost when our physicians abandoned Paris.

units.la: Les Assemblées se faisoient tousiours aux Maturins, d'autres chez le Doyen, ou bien chez l'ancien Maistre.
units.tr: The assemblies were always held at the Mathurins, though sometimes at the Dean's house or at the house of the senior master.

units.la: Les Leçons se faisoient en la maison des Maistres Regens, mesme les actes. La plus grande celebrité se faisoit dans la Sale de l'Evesché.
units.tr: The lectures were given in the houses of the regent masters, and the acts likewise. The greatest solemnity took place in the hall of the Bishop's palace.

units.la: Depuis ce temps-là les Medecins ont achepté deux maisons des Chartreux, où ils ont basty leur Escholé [?], en l'estat qu'elle est maintenant, à leurs despens, & l'ont toujours entretenuë.
units.tr: Since that time the physicians bought two houses from the Carthusians, where at their own expense they built their School [?] in the state in which it now is, and have always maintained it.

units.la: Aux nouvelles elections des Papes, pour lors residens en Avignon, l'Vniversité envoyoit un de chaque Faculté pour saluer le nouveau Pape, & conferer auec luy des affaires de l'Vniversité, & de l'Eglise.
units.tr: On the occasion of new elections of popes, who were then residing at Avignon, the University sent one from each Faculty to greet the new Pope and to confer with him about the affairs of the University and of the Church.

units.la: Il y auoit de ce temps-là deux Bedeaux, portans masses d'argent aux ceremonies.
units.tr: At that time there were two beadles, who carried silver maces at the ceremonies.

units.la: F I N.
units.tr: THE END.

units.la: Ie me fais fort, si l'Eschole de Montpelier doute de la fidelité de nos Registres, de les monstrer, & verifier, pourueu qu'ils nous monstrent les leurs, les Priuileges, & Lettres des Rois, qu'ils alleguent, que nous maintenons la pluspart estre fauses, ou sont données à toute l'Vniuersité de Montpelier.
units.tr: I undertake, if the Faculty of Montpellier doubts the fidelity of our Registers, to show and verify them, provided they show us theirs, the Privileges and Letters of the Kings which they allege; we maintain that most of them are false, or are granted to the whole University of Montpellier.

units.la: LEs Medecins Professeurs de l'Eschole de Montpelier demandent aux Docteurs de Paris, ce qu'ils n'ont iamais osé demander aux autres Vniuersitez; Ils font du ressort du Parlement de Thoulouse, & fort proches, Ils y vont souuent pour leurs differens; Toutesfois ils n'ont iamais demandé, ny l'aggregation, ny la préseance au College de Medecine de ladite Vniuersité, qui s'estime plus que celle de Montpelier pour l'antiquité, & pour la reputation qu'elle auoit du temps des premiers Cesars; & qui pour sa doctrine est appellée par Martial, Palladia Tholosa. Quand ledit Parlement a verifié quelques Lettres ou Priuileges de l'Escho-le de Montpelier, il a toujours adjousté en la verification, Sine prejudicio aliarum Facultatum Medicinæ, ne luy voulant donner aucune prerogatiue par dessus l'Eschole de Medecine de Thoulouse: Partant, que les Medecins Professeurs de Montpelier, nous monstrent des Arrests, qu'ils ont obtenus aux autres Parlemens, où il y a Université, ou College celebre, comme à Bordeaux, Aix, Roüen, Poictiers, Angers, pour preceder les Docteurs des Universitez de la Province, & y demeurer sans examen & approbation : Neantmoins, ils veulent obtenir dans Paris, ce qu'ils n'oseroient demander aux autres villes & Universitez. Pourquoy n'avez-vous point embrassé le procez d'un de vos Docteurs, nommé Cognard, à qui les Medecins de Roüen depuis peu ont refusé ignominieusement, l'aggregation & establissement dans leur ville, avec des invectives contre vostre Eschole, qui sont imprimées dans la Response qu'ils ont faite, au Factum de vostre Docteur, lequel sans doute vous les a envoyées, pour avoir vostre adionction en son procez, qu'il a perdu honteusement. A tout cela vous faites la sourde oreille, & dissimulez tout ce procedé, pour n'estre pas responsables de l'ignorance de vostre Docteur, qui estoit Compagnon Apothiquaire, & fils de Maistre, de la ville de Roüen.
units.tr: The Professors of medicine of the School of Montpellier ask of the Doctors of Paris what they have never dared to ask of the other Universities. They fall under the jurisdiction of the Parlement of Toulouse, and are very close to it; they go there often for their disputes. Yet they have never asked for either the aggregation or the precedence in the College of Medicine of that University, which esteems itself greater than that of Montpellier for its antiquity and for the reputation it had in the time of the first Caesars, and which, for its learning, is called by Martial Palladia Tholosa. Whenever the said Parlement has verified some letters or privileges of the School of Montpellier, it has always added to the verification Sine prejudicio aliarum Facultatum Medicinae, not wishing to grant it any prerogative over the School of Medicine of Toulouse. Therefore, let the Professors of medicine of Montpellier show us the decrees they have obtained in the other Parlements where there is a University or a celebrated College, such as Bordeaux, Aix, Rouen, Poitiers, Angers, that they may take precedence over the Doctors of the Universities of the Province and remain there without examination or approval. Nevertheless, they want to obtain in Paris what they would not dare to ask of the other cities and Universities. Why have you not taken up the lawsuit of one of your Doctors, named Cognard, whom the physicians of Rouen lately refused, shamefully, the aggregation and establishment in their city, with invectives against your School, which are printed in the Response they made to the Factum of your Doctor, which doubtless he sent you so as to have your support in his lawsuit, which he lost disgracefully. To all this you turn a deaf ear and dissemble all this proceeding, so as not to be answerable for the ignorance of your Doctor, who was a journeyman apothecary and the son of a master, from the city of Rouen.

units.la: l'apprens dans le livre du Sieur Ranchin, qu'il a composé de la Peste, que pas-vn Me decin de la ville de Montpelier ne s'est exposé,pour assister leurs Concitoyens: Ils y ont employé des Estrangers, & quand Ranchin s'est entremis de donner conseil pour le logement, & la nourriture, ç'a esté comme premier Viguier: mais quand il a fallu donner les moyens, de nettoyer & purifier la ville, on y a employé des Moines, pour donner l'instruction aux Medecins de Montpelier, qui ne connoissent pas les liures, qui ont esté faits par les Venitiens, & les Milanois, sur ce sujet.
units.tr: I learn from the book of Monsieur Ranchin, which he composed on the Plague, that not a single physician of the city of Montpellier exposed himself to assist their fellow citizens. They employed foreigners for this; and when Ranchin undertook to give advice on lodging and feeding, it was in his capacity as first Viguier. But when it came to providing the means to clean and purify the city, they employed monks to give instruction to the physicians of Montpellier, who do not know the books that were written on this subject by the Venetians and the Milanese.

units.la: Pag. 34. l. 13, apres deputez, adioustez.

units.la: Voyez le credit de l'Université de Paris aux affaires importantes de l'Eglise: En l'année 1402.le 27. de May, le Roy envoya une Lettre de cachet à chacune des Facultez de l'Université, pour avoir leur conseil, touchant les affaires de l'Eglise, qui estoit pour lors fort troublée, par les schismes & divisions des Antipapes. L'Université resolut, les quatre Facultez assemblées, de supplier le Roy de restablir & maintenir le Pape Benedictus treiziesme, ce qui fut executé ; la Lettre du Roy est inserée dans nos Registres. Nos Rois voulans reconnoistre par des gratifications signalées, l'affection que l'Vniuersité a toufiours porté à leur seruice, & au bien de l'Estat ; ils ont ordonné par Lettres Patentes, que l'Vniuersité, & toutes les Facultez, qui la composent, auront leurs causes commises pardeuant Monsieur le Preuost de Paris, Conseruateur de leurs priuileges ; ce qui a esté confirmé par le Roy François I. qui veut de plus, que les Cardinaux, s'ils ont quelque chose à demesler auec l'Vniuersité, viennent plaider pardeuant le Preuost de Paris: Monsieur le Cardinal de Gondy voulant tirer l'Vniuersité au Grand Conseil, par son Indult du Pape, il a esté iugé au Priué Conseil du Roy, l'an 1612. que les Priuileges de l'Vniuersité de Paris, sont preferables aux Iudults des Cardinaux.
units.tr: See the credit of the University of Paris in important affairs of the Church. In the year 1402, on the 27th of May, the King sent a letter under seal to each of the Faculties of the University, to obtain their counsel concerning the affairs of the Church, which was then greatly troubled by the schisms and divisions of the Antipopes. The University resolved, the four Faculties being assembled, to beg the King to restore and maintain Pope Benedict XIII, which was carried out; the King's letter is inserted in our Registers. Our Kings, wishing to acknowledge by notable favours the affection the University has always shown for their service and for the good of the State, have ordained by Letters Patent that the University, and all the Faculties which compose it, shall have their causes heard before the Provost of Paris, Conservator of their privileges; this was confirmed by King Francis I, who further wills that the Cardinals, if they have anything to dispute with the University, come to plead before the Provost of Paris. Monsieur the Cardinal de Gondi, wishing to draw the University before the Grand Council by his Papal indult, was judged in the King's Privy Council, in the year 1612, that the privileges of the University of Paris are to be preferred to the indults of the Cardinals.

units.la: Pline l'Oncle, Historia naturalis, lib.2.cap.63. nous aduertit, que la Nature ayant compassion de nos miseres, a produit les venins, comme des remedes à nos maux, pour en estre bien-toft deliurez, en nous donnant la mort, Naturam nostri misertam, venena instituisse credi potest; &c. Ita est, miserta genuit id, cuius facillimo haustu, illibato corpore, & cum toto sanguine extinguerémur[?]. Heresie abominable, qui a esté condamnée par les Chrestiens, mesmes par les Payens: Martial prononce là dessus son advis en homme de bien.
units.tr: Pliny the Elder, Historia naturalis, book 2, chapter 63, warns us that Nature, having compassion on our miseries, produced poisons as remedies for our ills, so that we might be quickly delivered by being given death: One may believe that Nature, taking pity on us, established poisons; etc. Yes indeed, in her compassion she produced that which, by a very easy draught, would extinguish us, with the body unharmed and with all the blood[?]. An abominable heresy, condemned by the Christians and even by the pagans. Martial gives his opinion on this matter like an honest man:

units.la: Rebus in adversis facile est contemnere mortem,Fortiùs ille facit, qui misèr esse potest.
units.tr: In adversity it is easy to despise death; he acts more bravely who can be wretched.

units.la: Les Loix punissent rigoureusement tels homicides, par confiscation de biens, & par ignominie horrible sur le corps mort. Neantmoins pour sortir honnestement hors de ce monde, la Chymie nous en fournit les moyens, sans crime,& sans soubçon de mort forcée, pour n'estre point declarez infames, & meurtriers, tant de la part du malade, que du Medecin, en prenant de l'Antimoine, sous pretexte d'une medecine excellente, qui terminera la maladie.
units.tr: The laws punish such homicides severely, by confiscation of goods and by a horrible ignominy inflicted on the dead body. Nevertheless, to leave this world honourably, chemistry supplies the means for us, without crime and without suspicion of forced death, so that neither the sick man nor the physician is declared infamous and a murderer, by taking antimony under the pretext of an excellent medicine which will end the illness.

units.la: Crede, & saluus eris, promisis certa fides, nam Cùm te interficient, morbo sanaberis omni.
units.tr: Believe, and you will be safe: the promise is sure, for when they kill you, you will be cured of every disease.

units.la: Ainsi un meschant homme se pourra defaire de sa femme, & une femme de son mary; de mesmes les heritiers pour avoir le bien, ou le benefice du malade, par l'entremise du Medecin Chymiste & Antimonial, se pourront defaire de quelqu'un, sans re proche de l'avoir fait mourir, ou avancé sa mort. O excellente Medecine, & à bon marché : aussi bien que le champignon de Claudius Cæsar, cibus deorum : puis qu'vn scrupule d'Antimoine vitrifié, ne coûte qu'vn denier, (la liure ne valant que quarante sols) suffisant toute-fois de faire mourir deux hommes, sans scrupule de conscience, ny sans aucun soubçon d'empoisonnement : Et voila ces gens qui meritent d'estre appellez Infames venefici.
units.tr: Thus a wicked man may rid himself of his wife, and a wife of her husband; likewise heirs, in order to gain the property or the benefice of the sick man, through the agency of the chemist and antimonial physician, may rid themselves of someone without reproach of having caused his death or hastened it. O excellent medicine, and cheap, like the mushroom of Claudius Caesar, food of the gods: since a scruple of vitrified antimony costs only a denier (the pound being worth only forty sols), and is enough to kill two men, without scruple of conscience and without any suspicion of poisoning. And here are these people who deserve to be called infamous poisoners.

units.la: Page 282. lig. 1. apres en mourut, adioustez dans Martial, Andragoras ne pouvant souffrir la laideur du visage du Medecin Hermocrates, apres avoir bien soupé, en songeant la nuit à ce Medecin, on le trouva le lendemain matin mort dans son lict.
units.tr: Page 282, line 1, after died of it, add: in Martial. Andragoras, unable to endure the ugliness of the face of the physician Hermocrates, after having dined well, dreaming at night of this physician, was found the next morning dead in his bed.

units.la: Lotus nobiscum est hilaris, cœnauit & idem, Inventus mane est mortuus Andragoras: Tam subita mortis causam Faustine, requiris, In somnis Medicum viderat Hermocratem.
units.tr: Lotus was with us, cheerful, and dined too; Andragoras was found dead in the morning. Faustinus, you ask the cause of so sudden a death: he had seen Hermocrates the physician in his dreams.

units.la: Page 190. lig. 9. rayez, de la qualité de.
units.tr: Page 190, line 9, strike out, of the quality of.
